translation.text:
After showing me these things[1], she wanted to run off. I say to her, "Lady, what profit is it to me to have seen these things and not know what the matters are?" Answering me, she says, "You are a crafty man, wanting to know the things concerning the tower." "Yes, lady," I say, "so that I may report them to the brothers, and that, becoming more cheerful and hearing these things, they may know the Lord in much glory."

She said, "Many indeed will hear; and, having heard, some of them will rejoice, but some will weep. But even these, if they hear and repent[b], they too will rejoice. Therefore listen to the parables of the tower, for I will reveal everything to you. And no longer cause me trouble about revelations, for these revelations have an end, for they have been completed. But you will not stop asking for revelations, for you are shameless."

"The tower that you see being built is I, the Church, the one shown to you both now and before. Whatever[2], therefore, you wish to inquire about the tower, I will reveal to you, so that you may rejoice with the holy ones."

I say to her, "Lady, since once for all you considered me worthy for everything to be revealed to me, reveal it." She says to me, "Whatever can be revealed to you will be revealed. Only let your heart be toward God, and do not be double-minded in whatever you see."

I asked her, "Why has the tower been built upon the waters, lady?" She says, "I told you before also, and you inquire diligently; therefore, by inquiring, you find the truth. Why, then, the tower has been built upon the waters—listen: because your life was saved through water and will be saved. And the tower has been founded by the word of the Almighty and glorious Name[a][9][8][7][6][5][4][3], and is held fast by the unseen power of the Master."

footnotes.text: Some witnesses include the clause "that they may become more cheerful, and"; others omit it.
"Parables" here refers to symbolic explanations of the vision’s elements, not necessarily short teaching stories.
"Are complete" could also be rendered "are fulfilled."
"Church" translates Ἐκκλησία, which could also mean "assembly" or "congregation"; here it is a personified title.
"Holy ones" is the literal sense of ἅγιοι and corresponds to the traditional "saints."
"Double-minded" echoes early Christian idiom (cf. James 1:8; 4:8) for inner division or wavering.
The saving "through water" strongly evokes baptism (cf. 1 Peter 3:20–21) in early Christian teaching.
"Name" is capitalized to reflect the reverential use of "the Name" for God in Jewish-Christian usage.
"Master" translates δεσπότης; some English versions use "Lord" here, but this rendering keeps it distinct from κύριος earlier in the sentence.
Or '"As for the tower that you see being built, I am the Church'.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: The tower represents the Church, personified as the woman speaking.
theological_decisions.rationale: The speaker self-identifies: "The tower that you see being built— I am the Church." The allegory is explicit in the text.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Capitalize "Name" as a reverential circumlocution for God.
theological_decisions.rationale: Jewish and early Christian usage treats "the Name" as a reverent stand-in for the divine; Hermas’s phrase "the Almighty and glorious Name" functions this way.

theological_decisions.issue: Scope of "these revelations have an end—they are complete"
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Refers to a finite set of visions in this cycle, not to the cessation of all revelation.
theological_decisions.rationale: Immediate context concerns Hermas’s persistent asking; "these revelations" points to a bounded series that are now complete, even if Hermas keeps asking.

theological_decisions.rationale: Maintains literalness while avoiding later ecclesiastical sense; readers can equivalently understand "saints."

review_passes.summary: The draft is highly accurate, preserving Hermas's register, moral pressure, and syntax well. One minor issue was found in verse 3, where an interpolated command ('ask') was added to an apodotic construction.
issues_found: Verse 3: The Greek `ὃ ἂν οὖν θελήσῃς ἐπερωτᾷν περὶ τοῦ πύργου, καὶ ἀποκαλύψω σοι` does not contain an imperative 'ask'. The `καὶ` is apodotic ('I will indeed reveal'). Adding 'ask, and' interpolates a command not present in the source.

revisions.to: "The tower that you see being built is I, the Church
revisions.rationale: Adjudicator-modified: The reviewer correctly notes that the Greek construction (a pendent nominative `ὁ μὲν πύργος` resumed by the predicate `ἐγώ εἰμι`) serves to directly identify the tower as the Church. The current rendering ('As for the tower... I am the Church') obscures this equation, making it sound like a non sequitur or a sudden change of topic. The proposed rewrite clarifies the predication, but 'is I' is preferable to 'is me' to maintain the appropriately elevated register of the visionary figure's speech

Ναί, φημί, κυρία, ἵνα τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀναγγείλω, καὶ [ἱλαρώτεροι γένωνται, καὶ ταῦτα] ἀκούσαντες γινώσκωσιν τὸν Κύριον ἐν πολλῇ δόξῃ. 2. ἡ δὲ ἔφη· Ἀκούσονται μὲν πολλοί· ἀκούσαντες δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν χαρήσονται, τινὲς δὲ κλαύσονται· ἀλλὰ καὶ οὗτοι, ἐὰν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ μετανοήσωσιν, καὶ αὐτοὶ χαρήσονται. ἄκουε οὖν τὰς παραβολὰς τοῦ πύργου· ἀποκαλύψω γάρ σοι πάντα. καὶ μηκέτι μοι κόπους πάρεχε περὶ ἀποκαλύψεως· αἱ γὰρ ἀποκαλύψεις αὗται τέλος ἔχουσιν· πεπληρωμέναι γάρ εἰσιν. ἀλλ’ οὐ παύσῃ αἰτούμενος ἀποκαλύψεις· ἀναιδὴς γὰρ εἶ. 3. ὁ μὲν πύργος ὃν βλέπεις οἰκοδομούμενον, ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ Ἐκκλησία, ἡ ὀφθεῖσά σοι καὶ νῦν καὶ τὸ πρότερον· ὃ ἂν οὖν AP. FATH. 20 θελήσῃς ἐπερωτᾷν περὶ τοῦ πύργου, καὶ ἀποκαλύψω σοι, ἵνα χαρῇς μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων. 4. λέγω αὐτῇ· Κυρία, ἐπεὶ ἅπαξ ἠξίών με ἠγήσω τοῦ πάντα μοι ἀποκαλῦψαι, ἀποκάλυψον. ἡ δὲ λέγει μοι· Ὃ ἐὰν ἐνδέχηταί σοι ἀποκαλυφθῆναι, ἀποκαλυφθήσεται. μόνον ἡ καρδία σου πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ἤτω καὶ μὴ διψυχήσῃς ὃ ἂν ἴδῃς. 5. ἐπηρώτησα αὐτήν· Διατί ὁ πύργος ἐπὶ ὑδάτων ᾠκοδόμηται, κυρία; Εἶπά σοι, φησίν, καὶ τὸ πρότερον, καὶ ἐκζητεῖς ἐπιμελῶς· ἐκζητῶν οὖν εὑρίσκεις τὴν ἀλήθειαν. διατί οὖν ἐπὶ ὑδάτων ᾠκοδόμηται ὁ πύργος, ἄκουε· ὅτι ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν διὰ ὕδατος ἐσώθη καὶ σωθήσεται. τεθεμελίωται δὲ ὁ πύργος τῷ ῥήματι τοῦ παντοκράτορος καὶ ἐνδόξου ὀνόματος, κρατεῖται δὲ ὑπὸ τῆς ἀοράτου δυνάμεως τοῦ δεσπότου.

translation.text: After showing me these things, she wanted to go away. I say to her, "Lady, what profit is it to me to have seen these things and not know what the matters are?" Answering me, she says, "You are a cunning man, wanting to know the things concerning the tower." "Yes, lady," I say, "so that I may report them to the brothers, and that, becoming more cheerful and hearing these things, they may know the Lord in much glory."

translation.text: She said, "Many indeed will hear; and, having heard, some of them will rejoice, but some will weep. But even these, if they hear and repent[a], they too will rejoice. Therefore listen to the parables of the tower, for I will reveal everything to you. And no longer cause me trouble about revelations, for these revelations have an end, for they have been completed. But you will not stop asking for revelations, for you are shameless."

Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it.

base_translation.text: After showing me these things, she wanted to go away. I say to her, "Lady, what profit is it to me to have seen these things and not know what the matters are?" Answering me, she says, "You are a cunning man, wanting to know the things concerning the tower." "Yes, lady," I say, "so that I may report them to the brothers, and that, becoming more cheerful and hearing these things, they may know the Lord in much glory."
